Navier–Stokes paper vs. Lean: Section 8 and Lemma 10.5 audit

Where the paper and its Lean formalization state things differently, extracted by a local model (3 independent samples per pair, kept separate) with every claim quoted and the quotes checked against the sources. This page lists differences. It does not say whether any difference matters. See METHODOLOGY.md. Paper: navier-stokes.pdf · Lean: openai/NavierStokesAndEuler at f9e8bc5b38b6

Retrospective recovery of two published discrepancies (Bastounis, Circelli & Hansen, arXiv:2610.08144): Lemma 8.6 (the paper loses m+4 derivatives, the Lean m+5) and eq. (10.19) inside the proof of Lemma 10.5 (the pressure-flux bound has a different first term). Lemma 8.6 and Lemma 10.5 were put on the target list because of that paper; no prompt mentions the discrepancies, the lemma, derivative counts or the bound.
  • Lemma 8.6: 3 of 3 samples reported a stronger-bound difference at SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.inverse_finiteJets, line 868. Control: the same check fires on 0 of the other 66 pairs, and on 0 of 606 windows (0.0%) along their statements.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: 3 of 3 samples reported a other / stronger-bound / weaker-bound difference at PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, lines 587-588. Control: the same check fires on 60 of the other 66 pairs, and on 199 of 530 windows (37.5%) along their statements.

Grouped differences at the target lines:

  • Lemma 8.6: SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.inverse_finiteJets, 3/3 samples, SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean:868: The paper's derivative loss is m+4, while the Lean theorem assumes n+5 and concludes n.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 1/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:588: If the quantities correspond, the Lean bound has an additional positive 1/R^2 contribution not present in the paper's displayed bound.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 1/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:587: The paper's cutoff notation is χ_R/φ_R; the Lean statement uses ComparisonCutoffs.weight/cutoff.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 0/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:587-588: The algebraic form of the first part of the bound differs.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 0/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:588: The Lean expression includes an additional 1/R^2 summand.
